description.value: A voxel-based morphometric study comparing gray matter volume between methadone maintenance patients with heroin dependence and healthy controls, and examining associations with depression, anxiety, and cognitive performance.

spans.text: We investigated differences in gray matter volume (GMV) between 27 MMT patients and 23 healthy controls with voxel-based morphometry, and we correlated findings in the patients with Beck Depression Inventory scores, Beck Anxiety Inventory scores, and diminished cognitive functioning.

value: At the uncorrected p < 0.001 threshold, MMT patients showed extensively smaller GMV in the frontal lobe, including the left medial frontal cortex, left inferior frontal gyrus, and right inferior frontal gyrus; the left sub-callosal cingulate gyrus, left anterior cingulate gyrus, postcentral gyrus, bilateral insula, left cerebellar vermis, and right cerebellar declive also showed significantly smaller GMV.
These structural deficits were associated with the severity of depression, anxiety, and cognitive dysfunction.

spans.text: By using a p value of 0.001 (uncorrected), the MMT patients showed extensively smaller GMV in the frontal lobe, including the left medial frontal cortex (BA 9), left inferior frontal gyrus (BA 47), and right inferior frontal gyrus (BA 11). The MMT patients also showed significantly smaller GMV in the left sub-callosal cingulate gyrus (BA 32), left anterior cingulate gyrus (BA 25), postcentral gyrus (BA 3), and bilateral insula (BA 13). Aside from cerebral deficits, there was significantly smaller GMV in the left cerebellar vermis and the right cerebellar declive.

The Chang Gung Memorial Hospital human research committee approved the study protocol.

From March 2009 to February 2010, 27 patients with heroin dependence (26 males, 1 female, median age 37 years, range 23–53 years) attending the psychiatric department of a tertiary referral center hospital for methadone maintenance therapy (MMT) were prospectively enrolled.
Because of male predominance in the enrolled groups, the effect of gender on GMV needs further analysis.

The MMT participants met the DSM-IV criteria for opiate dependence within 2 years before the study, had been on a stable dose of methadone within half a year preceding the study, and had been illicit drug-free for the last 12 months.

spans.text: The MMT participants met the DSM-IV criteria for opiate dependence within 2 years before the study, had been on a stable dose of methadone within half a year preceding the study, and had been illicit drug-free for the last 12 months. They were also required to have negative urine toxicology screening tests (excluding methadone) as reported in their treatment programs.

spans.text: The exclusionary criteria included current or lifetime history of any Axis I diagnosis (other than opiate dependence and nicotine use), current alcohol intake greater than 15 drinks (1.5 oz liquor, 12 oz beer, or 5 oz wine equivalents) per week, history of head trauma or neurologic disease, and HIV seropositivity. Heroin-induced depressive syndrome was the only depressive disorder history allowed in the patients. Nine patients exhibited axis I depressive illness before heroin use and were excluded. Cognitive impairment induced by acute doses of benzodiazepines was well documented, so potential participants with a history of recent benzodiazepine use or a current diagnosis of sedative/hypnotic dependence (based on self-reports and clinical records) were also excluded.
